identity.name: Candelilla wax
identity.chemical_class: Natural plant wax (primarily hydrocarbons with esters and free acids)

function.mechanism: Forms a hydrophobic surface film and reduces surface friction/stickiness, improving gloss and handling stability.

adi.basis: EFSA 2012 re-evaluation concluded there was no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses and use levels.

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern at reported uses/use levels; no numerical ADI required.

fda.notes: Direct human food ingredient affirmed as GRAS under GMP; functional use as lubricant and surface-finishing agent; listed food uses include chewing gum and hard candy.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED and notes no safety concern at predicted dietary exposure (<650 mg/person/day).

concerns.summary: No strong recent hazard signal was identified, but modern dedicated toxicology/epidemiology data specific to E902 are limited.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2012 re-evaluation reported no safety concern at reported uses/use levels and no need for a numerical ADI.
JECFA lists ADI as not specified with no safety concern at predicted exposure in its evaluation context.
No IARC classification entry was identified for candelilla wax in the checked IARC classification dataset.

adi_exceedance.notes: Given ADI-not-specified conclusions from EFSA and JECFA and current permitted uses, routine dietary exceedance concern is low in available evidence.

risk_assessment.rationale: Convergent regulatory conclusions (EFSA, FDA/eCFR, JECFA) support low concern at intended uses, but evidence is driven mainly by regulatory dossiers and there is limited recent epidemiological/toxicological literature specific to E902.
key_factors: EFSA re-evaluation found no safety concern and no numerical ADI need
FDA affirms GRAS status in 21 CFR 184.1976 with GMP conditions
JECFA lists ADI not specified and no safety concern at predicted exposure
Sparse modern dedicated hazard studies specific to candelilla wax
